archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-propped)
archetype.definition: A Metropolitan also-ran that is close enough to .500 to stay in the race, but is getting outshot and out-chanced and leans on one goalie and a thin top of the lineup to stay level.

report.headline: Talbot is holding up a team that's lost last year's edge at five-on-five
report.take:
Columbus sits sixth in the Metropolitan at 7-8-0, 24th on the site, on pace for 77 standings points. That would be a step back from a club that had climbed to 89 and then 92 points over the last two seasons. The record is honest. Its Pts vs Goal Diff is -0.3, so it isn't losing a stack of coin flips, and it has no overtime losses at all. The -7 goal differential and 25th-ranked Goal Diff / GP describe a team that is a little worse than its opponents most nights.

The real change from last year is territory. Last season the Blue Jackets won the 5-on-5 chance battle with a 52% xGF share. This year they are at 48.2% xGF and 48% CF, both in the low 20s league-wide, and they put only 25.8 shots a game on net against 27.9 allowed. Add a power play converting 17.5%, 26th in the league, and a skater shooting percentage of 9.8% against a league mark of 11.6%, and you get an offense ranked 29th at 2.67 goals a game. Defensively they are a middling 18th, and that is mostly thanks to the crease. Team GSAx of 4.6 ranks 9th, and Cam Talbot alone accounts for more than that at 5.6 GSAx with a .911 save percentage. Jet Greaves has made more starts and sits at .880 and -1.6.

The numbers hide two things. First, the finishing slump is not a 5-on-5 bad-luck story. 5-on-5 PDO is a near-neutral 99.8, but all-situations PDO is 99.3 against a league 100.6, which points the finger at the power play and at forwards who aren't converting. Adam Fantilli leads the forwards with 45 shots but has 4 goals. Conor Garland has none on 18 shots and Sean Monahan one. Some of that comes back. Second, the recent trend is a bit better than the record says. Over the last ten they allowed 2.6 a game and over the last five the differential was even, though a 7-2 win over Colorado does a lot of that lifting.

The top of the lineup works. Kent Johnson has 16 points, Charlie Coyle has 13 with a 56.7% xGF share, and Zach Werenski is logging 28.3 minutes with 14 points. The forward group still grades D+, and the third pair is getting buried. That is a profile that hovers just under the playoff line unless the shooting turns and Talbot keeps this up.

strengths.title: Talbot is stealing goals
strengths.body: Cam Talbot has been one of the league's better goalies, 10th on the goalie tab with a .911 save percentage and 5.6 GSAx. That is why a team that gives up more shots than it takes still ranks 9th in team GSAx and 11th in save percentage. A goalie running this far above expected usually comes back some. Last season's 7.8 team GSAx says this crease can be a real asset, but not necessarily at this level all year.

strengths.title: A real top tier: Werenski, Johnson, Coyle
strengths.body: Werenski plays 28.3 minutes a night, ranks 23rd among defensemen and has 14 points. Kent Johnson leads the team with 16 points and ranks 33rd among centers. Coyle has driven play best of anyone, with a 56.7% xGF share alongside 13 points. This is production from players carrying heavy minutes, so it should hold. The problem is how quickly the quality drops off behind them.

concerns.title: Last year's 5-on-5 gains have vanished
concerns.body: The 2025-26 team won the expected-goals battle at 52%. This one sits at 48.2%, 22nd, and is out-shot by a wide margin. That is the root of the 25th-ranked Goal Diff / GP, and it is a play-driving problem, not a bounce problem. Without a recovery here, even better finishing only gets them to mediocre.

concerns.title: Power play and finishing are cold
concerns.body: A 17.5% power play, 26th and well under the league's 22.5%, combines with 9.8% shooting to produce the 29th-ranked offense. 5-on-5 PDO is basically average, so most of the drought is on special teams and in individual conversion. Fantilli, Garland and Monahan are the obvious names. Shooting should drift up toward the league norm, but the power play has not been good in any of the last five seasons, so don't expect a full fix there.

concerns.title: The bottom pair and the other goalie
concerns.body: Erik Gudbranson is -9 with a 41.8% xGF share and ranks 231st of 252 defensemen. Carson Soucy is worse by tab rank, and Jake Christiansen is also under water. Greaves's .880 over a near-even share of the starts gives back much of what Talbot earns. If the goaltending evens out without the third pair improving, goals against will climb.

trend.note: A 5-7 October gave way to a 2-1 start to November, and the last ten went 5-5 with goals against trending down. The record itself has barely moved off .500, and several of the wins came by a goal in overtime.

weekAhead.headline: Two puck-hogs, then Philadelphia: a homestand that tests the shot deficit
weekAhead.body:
All three games are at home, but the first two are against teams that live in the offensive zone. Florida ranks 4th in CF% at 55% and allows only 23.9 shots a game. Tampa Bay is 4th in xGF% at 56% with A-grade forwards and an A+ blueline. For a Columbus team already losing the shot battle, those two nights hinge on Talbot and on converting the few looks it gets. Florida's 85.7% penalty kill shuts the door on a struggling power play.

Philadelphia on Saturday is the reprieve. The Flyers are 4-10-5, 30th on the site, 30th in xGF% and 31st in offense, with an F-grade forward group. That is a game Columbus has to bank, and its defensemen should feast: Philadelphia gives up more points to blueliners above expectation than all but two teams. A split of the first two plus a win over the Flyers would be a good week. One point from the first two is the likelier result.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's leaky penalty kill
keyMatchups.body: Tampa Bay's PK sits at 72.9%, 24th, and its goalies have a .882 save percentage, 25th, with negative GSAx. Its record also runs ahead of its goals, at +2.2 Pts vs Goal Diff. If Columbus's power play is going to break out, the Lightning are the team to do it against. Florida's 85.7% kill two nights earlier is the opposite.

keyMatchups.title: Werenski against soft blue-line coverage
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia ranks 30th and Tampa 28th at holding defensemen under their expected points. Werenski, at 28.3 minutes with 14 points, and Mateychuk, with 4 goals, are positioned to cash in. Columbus's offense needs its back end to generate, given how cold the forwards' shooting has been.

keyMatchups.title: Who starts in goal
keyMatchups.body: The gap between Talbot's .911 and Greaves's .880 is the biggest swing on this roster. Against Florida and Tampa, who will out-shoot Columbus, the starter matters more than usual. Greaves getting one of those two nights tilts the week toward tough.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Columbus can keep shots close against Florida and Tampa, or whether it is once again asking its goalie to win games it is losing on the ice.

restOfSeason.body:
The 77-point pace is a fair baseline, and there is a little upside in it. Skater shooting at 9.8% is unlikely to stay that far under the league's 11.6%, especially with Fantilli putting pucks on net. A modest power-play recovery would push scoring toward the high-2s or 3 goals a game. Pulling the other way, Talbot's 5.6 GSAx is a hot run that rarely lasts a full season, and Greaves has been below average. Without better goaltending from him, the defense could slip from its middling 18th.

The decider is five-on-five. This core reached 52% xGF last year, so a rebound is plausible, but nothing in the last ten games shows it yet. I see a team finishing somewhere around 78 to 86 points: in the conversation for a wild card in a Metro where Carolina and New Jersey have pulled away, but more likely just outside it.
swingFactors: Talbot sustaining above-expected goaltending or Greaves stabilizing
A return toward last year's 52% xGF share
Power-play and forward shooting regression upward

confidence.note: 15 games is a small sample, but the shot and chance shares, goalie split and history all point the same way.
